revision_note: v2 (2026-10-08): re-verified after the IR-54-021 continuation-direction fix (one-sided -> two-sided outward tip continuations) and the IR-54-022 receipt-schema compliance fix. All holdout numbers, the random control, the raster, and the lane figures below are the post-fix values. The superseded pre-fix receipt is evidence/cgrc_holdout_receipt_v1_superseded.json.
hypothesis: The competition catalogue is a fragmented digitisation (3,118 kept components, median 12 cells, 6,747 degree-1 tips on a 100 m grid). The canonical reason a national compilation misses a fault is a relay/stepover geometry: the short segment linking two mapped, roughly parallel, facing tips is exactly the low-displacement strand that drops out of the compilation. The gaps between facing catalogue tips are therefore higher-precision candidates for expert-labelled 'new' faults than the bulk off-catalogue surface that the dotted family covers.
mechanism: CGRC (Catalogue Gap Relay Completion): straight relay lines between tips of different catalogue components whose strikes agree (<=25 deg), tips face each other along the shared strike, lateral stepover <= 500 m, gap 100-2500 m and empty of catalogue cells; plus TWO-SIDED outward tangent continuations of every segment end up to 2500 m (the IR-54-021 fix - each end extends away from the segment interior, not both ends in one strike-signed direction). Candidate cells are the 2 px scaffold around those lines, excluded from the 200 m catalogue zone (the dotted-family prune threshold; the 300 m exclusion collapses the mechanism, see evidence/cgrc_holdout_receipt_excl300_band-collapse.json). Dots by metric-optimal greedy packing, one per 300 m kernel width. The shipped arm is B (SGMC corroboration in placement priority): after the IR-54-021 re-verification B = 0.091536 is significantly above A (pure catalogue) = 0.090341 (paired 95% CI [-0.002163, -0.000204] excludes 0), so the SGMC-corroborated placement ships.
named_non_fault_process_that_could_mimic: Digitisation artefacts and non-fault line work: (a) fault strands that terminate at map-sheet boundaries or lithologic contacts and do not actually continue (the continuation lines then predict a phantom segment); (b) en-echelon patterns that are actually separate short faults with no linking relay (relay lines then cross a gap that contains no fault); (c) graben-bounding normal-fault pairs of different age whose tips are geometrically facing but tectonically unrelated; (d) pre-Quaternary (Tertiary) structures with no geothermal expression. The empty-gap + strike-compatibility + facing-tip gates remove (a)-(c) only to the extent the geometry is clean; item (d) is NOT removed and is the main reason the artefact could underperform.

holdout_dti.label: HOLDOUT-DTI (catalogue-truth proxy; cannot reward genuinely new off-catalogue faults)
holdout_dti.design: whole fault segments withheld in 4 spatial quadrant folds + 300 m buffer; features from visible catalogue only (pixel-exact); pooled DTI alpha 0.2 beta 0.8 300 m triangular kernel; whole-segment cluster bootstrap n=2000; bootstrap algebra self-checked to reproduce the organizer metric exactly (full-draw replicate == headline, 1e-6); receipt passes scripts/analyse_holdout_receipt.py
holdout_dti.exclusion300_collapse_note: At a 300 m catalogue exclusion the mechanism's operating band (the 200-300 m gap zone between visible tips and withheld segments) is excluded from candidates and recovery collapses (0.0753 -> 0.0042 on the 1.5 km baseline family). This proves the 200 m exclusion is not a tuning artifact but the mechanism's geometry.
holdout_dti.ir_54_021_note: The corrected two-sided outward continuation adds off-catalogue mass that the on-catalogue proxy truth cannot reward: the pre-fix one-sided variant scored 0.109072 (22,352 dots, 2.47x random) and the post-fix two-sided variant scores 0.091536 (32,529 dots, 1.50x random). This is the catalogue-truth proxy's known bias against off-catalogue mass (IR-32-PROXY-01 class), NOT evidence that the pre-fix geometry was better on the off-catalogue task. The proxy cannot score the off-catalogue gaps/continuations the method is built to predict.
holdout_dti.status: ESTABLISHED on the catalogue-truth proxy; NOT a competition score and NOT a projection of one

question_0.0028.detail: 0.2778 vs 0.2750 (gap 0.0028) is 2.0x the raw-scale MDE (0.001395) of a same-method-family paired contrast on a holdout with 60,834 withheld positives and 3,118 whole-segment units: such a gap is detectable (power > 0.8) if the two candidates are compared paired on the same holdout draws. It is NOT detectable as an architecture-level ranking: distinct-architecture contrasts carry far larger paired variance (the circular SGMC proxy measured sigma 0.31-0.47, i.e. MDE ~0.012-0.018), so reading 0.0028 as evidence that one architecture beats another is reading noise. The earlier proxy-only analysis (evidence/power_analysis.json) is superseded by this whole-segment measurement for same-family contrasts.

leakage_canary.note: No single-feature leakage above 0.90. The SGMC layer is only weakly pixel-aligned with the catalogue, so the catalogue-truth proxy is not circular for this method (contrast with the H54-A SGMC-complement candidate, whose SGMC-alone AUC was 0.998 against an SGMC-derived target). Using SGMC as a placement corroboration weight is therefore not a leakage shortcut; its value is measured by the arm A/B contrast below.

correlation_overlap_vs_registry.closest_non_vacuous_registry: hedge_v2_01563.tif (0.5613 at 2.5 km extent, two-sided continuation)
correlation_overlap_vs_registry.vacuity_proof: The three flagged rasters blanket 73.97% / 99.87% / 76.20% of the study footprint within 3 px of their dots (evidence/cgrc_submission_receipt.json, lane_infeasibility_proof). Satisfying the 70% rule against r13 would require >30% of a submission's dots to sit in the 0.13% of the footprint outside r13's 3-px zone - a degenerate boundary sliver no non-degenerate fault prediction can occupy. The rule is therefore unsatisfiable by any real submission against these three rasters (a protocol defect flagged in docs/audit/irregularities.md, IR-54-016); the operational lane test is the rank-correlation condition (max |rho| = 0.0422, 21x below the 0.90 limit) plus the 3-px rule against the nine non-vacuous rasters (all pass, max 0.5613).

score_model_range.label: MODEL (not a score, not a projection written as a score)
score_model_range.assumptions: hidden truth mass G ~ 11,583 cells (algebraic inverse of two owner-recorded, unreceipted board rows on the dotted family - see docs/research/why-h33.md); credit coverage on the hidden truth at the proxy-measured level. The catalogue-truth proxy understates an off-catalogue method, so the true board value is uncertain and could be above or below the proxy.
score_model_range.note: Below the corpus best (0.2778) and the prompt's 0.3195 target; the proxy cannot certify the off-catalogue gaps/continuations, so the range is wide.

verdict_rationale: The artefact is unique and lane-clean and its surface beats mass-matched random on the whole-segment holdout (1.50x, self-checked against the organizer metric). But the protocol gate 'do not spend a submission slot on an idea that hasn't beaten the current holdout best' is not met: 0.0915 < 0.1793 (GEMSDOE32's greedy-surface arm on the same catalogue-truth task class). Two honest caveats: (1) the catalogue-truth proxy systematically penalizes the off-catalogue mass this method emits, so the holdout is a lower bound on the off-catalogue task, not a fair score of it; (2) the pre-fix one-sided geometry scored 0.1091 on the same proxy only because it emitted less off-catalogue mass - that is the proxy's bias, not a better method. Promotion to a real slot is a separate selector step; if the selector values portfolio diversity (a distinct-lane mechanism probe), this artefact is the candidate - otherwise do not spend a weekly slot this week.

experiments: E1 whole-segment hide-and-recover holdout, 4 spatial folds + 300 m buffer, arms A/B, cluster bootstrap, leakage canary (incl. the 300 m-exclusion band-collapse diagnostic and the mass-matched random control)
E2 lane-safety configuration selection: 1.5 km vs 2.5 km relay/continuation extent at 200 m exclusion, pre-placement and final-dot lane checks against all 12 registry rasters
budget_used.note: Within the 3-experiment / 2-hour budget. The IR-54-021 continuation-direction fix triggered a re-verification of the same two configurations (pass-2, not a new experiment) plus a pass-2 receipt-schema compliance fix (IR-54-022); no new parameter tuning (avoids proxy overfitting).

negative_results_companion: A 300 m catalogue exclusion collapses CGRC (0.0753 -> 0.0042 on the 1.5 km baseline): the relay/continuation mechanism operates in the 200-300 m band around the catalogue, the same band the dotted family empirically validated for retention (0.2600 -> 0.2778 prune).

IR-54-021: the one-sided continuation direction bug made the pre-fix artefact score HIGHER on the catalogue-truth proxy (0.1091, 2.47x random) purely by emitting less off-catalogue mass. The corrected two-sided artefact scores 0.0915 (1.50x random). The proxy cannot arbitrate the off-catalogue bet; both values are proxy artefacts, not off-catalogue scores.

SGMC-corroborated placement (arm B) now SIGNIFICANTLY beats pure catalogue geometry (arm A) on the corrected geometry: 0.091536 vs 0.090341, paired 95% CI [-0.002163, -0.000204] excludes 0. The pre-fix geometry showed no significant difference (delta +0.00001). The SGMC-corroborated arm ships.

The parallel-run lane rule's 3-px overlap condition is unsatisfiable against the three near-blanking registry rasters (r11/r13/r14 cover 74-99.87% of the footprint within 3 px); any submission, whatever its method, trips it. Flagged as a protocol defect (IR-54-016); the rank-correlation condition is the operational method-similarity test.
